name: German Solo
description: German Solo is a four-player trick-taking game from the Ombre family with contract bidding, temporary partnerships, and a fixed high-trump structure built around matadors.
deck: 32-card deck (A K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

overview.description: German Solo is a four-player trick-taking game from the Ombre family with contract bidding, temporary partnerships, and a fixed high-trump structure built around matadors.
overview.deck: 32-card deck (A K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

history.origins: German Solo emerged as a simplified descendant of l'Hombre and Quadrille. It later persisted mainly in regional communities in the United States.
timeline: 18th to 19th century: Ombre descendants spread through Europe.
19th century: German Solo forms as a practical bidding-trick variant.
20th century onward: Survives in US local circles while fading in Germany.
history.cultural: Often taught as a heritage game linking modern partnership contracts to older Ombre mechanics.
history.evolution: Contract names and scoring details vary by table, but core features remain fixed: matador trumps, bid ladder, and trick contracts with or without partner calls.

setup.deck: 32-card stripped pack: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit.
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards to each player, commonly in a 3-2-3 or 4-2-2 pattern.
setup.equipment: Score sheet or chips for bid-value settlement.

rules.objective: As bidder or bidder side, complete contract trick target; as defenders, set the contract.
rules.gameplay: Players bid once in turn with higher contracts over lower. Some contracts create a temporary partner via called ace or king; others are solo contracts. Winning bid determines trump suit and contract objective. Play 8 tricks with follow-suit required. If void in led suit, player may trump or discard. Highest trump wins trick; otherwise highest of led suit. Trick winner leads next.
keyRules: Matador order is fixed: club queen highest, then seven of trump, then spade queen, followed by remaining trump hierarchy.
Contracts form a ladder and determine target tricks, trump regime, and whether bidder plays alone or with called partner.
Each player bids at most once per hand in the common four-player form.
Settlement is by bid value transfer with optional table bonuses such as mackers and first-and-last.

strategy.basic: Count top trumps early and avoid overbidding without at least five probable tricks in solo contracts.
strategy.intermediate: When calling a partner card, choose a suit call that helps establish side-suit winners rather than only immediate trump control.
strategy.advanced: Exploit matador timing by withholding or forcing key trumps to control who reaches end-trick lead transitions.
tips: Do not treat fixed matadors as ordinary suit cards during trick evaluation.
Track remaining trumps by contract because trump count differs by selected suit.

variations.name: Six-Hand Solo
variations.description: A faster six-player variant using card removals and five-card hands; strategy differs from core four-player form.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Six-hand uses different player count and deal; overrides can be added when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Macker Bonuses
variations.description: Optional bonus payouts for holding first three, four, or five top matador sequence cards under contract conditions.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional bonus rules vary by table; add overrides when encoding specific bonus values.

variations.name: First and Last
variations.description: Optional payout bonus for capturing first five tricks and potentially last three under eligible contracts.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional first-last bonus rules vary by table; add overrides when encoding specific payout.

scoring.description: Contract winner side wins or loses hand value based on meeting trick target; many tables include optional macker and first-last bonuses.
scoring.winCondition: Complete your declared contract target; otherwise defenders set and collect.

synthesis.shortDescription: Four-player contract trick game with fixed high matadors and temporary partner calls.
